concepts.name: Definition and Core Principles of Green Economy
key_dimensions: UNEP's definition vs. broader interpretations (low-carbon, resource-efficient, socially inclusive)
Distinction between Green Economy and Sustainable Development — overlap and divergence
Trap: Green Economy ≠ Green Growth ≠ Circular Economy — subtle definitional differences
Criticism: 'Green Economy' as a developed-world construct imposing constraints on developing nations

concepts.name: Green GDP and Natural Capital Accounting
key_dimensions: Concept of adjusting GDP to account for environmental degradation and resource depletion
System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) — UN framework and India's adoption status
Limitations of Green GDP as a welfare measure vs. alternatives like Genuine Savings/Adjusted Net Savings (World Bank)
Trap: Green GDP is not an official metric used by most countries — contrast with HDI or GNH

concepts.name: Carbon Pricing Mechanisms: Carbon Tax vs. Cap-and-Trade
key_dimensions: Structural difference: Carbon tax = price certainty; Cap-and-trade = quantity certainty
EU Emissions Trading System (EU-ETS) as the world's largest carbon market — design and lessons
India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) 2023 under Energy Conservation Act — key features
Trap: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) of EU — implications for Indian exports, not a domestic carbon price

concepts.name: Green Finance: Instruments and Architecture
key_dimensions: Green Bonds vs. Sustainability Bonds vs. Social Bonds — definitional traps and use-of-proceeds rules
India's Sovereign Green Bond Framework — sectors eligible, use of proceeds, SEBI taxonomy
Role of NGFS (Network for Greening the Financial System) and climate-related financial risk disclosure
Trap: Green bonds do not guarantee environmental outcomes — 'greenwashing' risk and verification gap

concepts.name: Circular Economy vs. Linear Economy
key_dimensions: 3R hierarchy (Reduce → Reuse → Recycle) vs. 9R framework of circular economy
Ellen MacArthur Foundation's model — biological and technical cycles
India's Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) rules under Plastic Waste, E-waste, Battery Waste regulations
Trap: Recycling is the last resort in circular economy, not the primary strategy — misconception in prelims options

concepts.name: Renewable Energy Transition and Green Economy Linkages
key_dimensions: India's NDC targets vs. installed capacity milestones — 500 GW non-fossil by 2030
Green jobs creation potential vs. just transition challenge for fossil-fuel-dependent workers/regions
Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for solar modules and its green economy rationale
Trap: Renewable energy alone does not constitute a green economy — demand-side efficiency equally critical

concepts.name: Green Taxonomy and ESG Frameworks
key_dimensions: Purpose of green taxonomy: defining what economic activities qualify as 'environmentally sustainable'
EU Taxonomy Regulation — 6 environmental objectives and 'Do No Significant Harm' (DNSH) principle
India's status: No official green taxonomy yet — SEBI's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) as proxy
Trap: ESG rating agencies are private; no global regulatory standard — scores vary significantly across agencies

concepts.name: Ecosystem Services Valuation and Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES)
key_dimensions: TEEB (The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity) framework — four categories of ecosystem services
Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES): conditionality, additionality, and permanence principles
India's Compensatory Afforestation Fund (CAMPA) as quasi-PES mechanism — criticisms of its effectiveness
Trap: Ecosystem valuation ≠ commodification — the philosophical debate often appears in ethics/mains context

concepts.name: Just Transition: Social Dimension of Green Economy
key_dimensions: ILO's Just Transition Guidelines — link between decent work, social protection, and decarbonization
Coal-dependent regions in India (Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh) — displacement and reskilling challenges
Differentiation: Just Transition for workers vs. Just Transition for developing nations (CBDR principle)
Trap: 'Just Transition' is not merely an environmental concept — it is fundamentally a social equity framework

concepts.name: Green Public Procurement (GPP)
key_dimensions: Definition: Government using purchasing power to choose environmentally preferable goods and services
India's initiatives: BEE star-labelled products, LED procurement under EESL, GeM portal's green category
GPP as a demand-side policy instrument vs. supply-side instruments like subsidies
Trap: GPP is voluntary in most countries including India — mandatory only in specific sectors/EU member states

concepts.name: Carbon Markets: Voluntary vs. Compliance Markets
key_dimensions: Compliance markets (legally mandated) vs. Voluntary Carbon Markets (VCM) — key structural differences
Article 6 of Paris Agreement — internationally transferred mitigation outcomes (ITMOs) and double-counting trap
India's forest carbon credits and REDD+ mechanism — eligibility and accounting rules
Trap: Voluntary carbon offsets do not count toward national NDC targets unless linked to Article 6.2 mechanisms

concepts.name: Sustainable Finance and Climate Risk: Physical vs. Transition Risk
key_dimensions: Physical risk (acute: floods, chronic: sea-level rise) vs. Transition risk (policy, technology, market shifts)
Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) — four pillars: governance, strategy, risk management, metrics
RBI's draft framework on climate risk and sustainable finance for Indian banks (2023)
Trap: Transition risk can arise even from climate action (stranded assets) — not only from climate inaction

concepts.name: Sustainable Agriculture and Green Economy: Agroecology vs. Climate-Smart Agriculture
key_dimensions: Agroecology principles vs. Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) — FAO frameworks and philosophical differences
India's schemes: Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF), Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
Carbon sequestration in agricultural soils — '4 per 1000' initiative and India's participation
Trap: Climate-Smart Agriculture is criticized for accommodating GMOs and industrial farming — not universally 'green'

concepts.name: Sustainable Urban Infrastructure: Green Buildings and Smart Cities
key_dimensions: GRIHA (Green Rating for Integrated Habitat Assessment) — India's national green building rating vs. LEED (US-based)
Energy Conservation Building Code (ECBC) — mandatory vs. voluntary applicability across building types
Net-Zero Energy Buildings (NZEB) concept and India's roadmap under BEE
Trap: GRIHA is developed by TERI and administered by ADaRSH — not directly by the government; LEED is a US private standard

concepts.name: Biodiversity and Natural Capital in Green Economy
key_dimensions: Dasgupta Review (2021): Treating nature as an asset — 'inclusive wealth' framework
Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) 30x30 target — link to green economy financing
Biodiversity credits as emerging instrument — distinction from carbon credits
Trap: Biodiversity credits are not the same as carbon credits — biodiversity loss cannot be 'offset' by carbon sequestration alone

concepts.name: Green Economy and Trade: WTO Compatibility and Green Protectionism
key_dimensions: EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) — sectors covered (steel, cement, aluminum, fertilizers, electricity, hydrogen)
WTO's GATT Article XX exceptions for environmental measures — 'necessary' test and non-discrimination
India's position: CBAM as 'green protectionism' violating CBDR principle
Trap: CBAM is a trade measure, not a climate finance instrument — revenues go to EU budget, not to developing country climate funds

concepts.name: Waste-to-Resource Economy: Municipal Solid Waste and Industrial Symbiosis
key_dimensions: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 — EPR for waste generators, source segregation mandate
Industrial symbiosis: Kalundborg (Denmark) model — waste of one industry as input for another
Waste-to-Energy (WtE) plants — controversy: incineration lock-in vs. circular economy principles
Trap: Waste-to-Energy is NOT circular economy — it is end-of-pipe and lower in the waste hierarchy than reuse/recycle

concepts.name: International Frameworks and Institutions Driving Green Economy
key_dimensions: UNEP's Green Economy Initiative vs. OECD's Green Growth Strategy — similarities and key differences in approach
Green Climate Fund (GCF) — governance structure, mitigation vs. adaptation funding balance, India's access
Global Environment Facility (GEF) vs. GCF — mandate overlap, focal areas, and trap on which funds what
Trap: GEF funds biodiversity, land degradation, chemicals too — not only climate; GCF is exclusively climate-focused

concepts.name: Energy Efficiency as a Green Economy Pillar: Standards and Labeling
key_dimensions: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) — statutory body under Energy Conservation Act 2001 (amended 2022)
UJALA scheme, EESL, and Perform Achieve Trade (PAT) scheme — mechanism of tradable energy saving certificates (ESCerts)
Energy Conservation Amendment Act 2022 — carbon market provisions, green hydrogen mandate, energy efficiency in buildings
Trap: ESCerts under PAT are different from carbon credits under CCTS — PAT is energy efficiency; CCTS is GHG emissions-based
